why: #396. Filed as a same-file `IMPLEMENTS` resolution defect ("a supertype declared in the same file as its subtype produces no edge") — but `_resolve_type`'s same-package guess makes no distinction between same-file and same-package-different-file, and there was never a code path matching that description. What actually reproduces the filed repro is a `tree-sitter-kotlin` 1.1.0 scanner ambiguity: `interface Iface { fun f() }` — a single-line body whose only member has no explicit return type — immediately followed by another single-line declaration collapses the *entire rest of the file* into one `ERROR` node, losing every declaration in it, not just the `IMPLEMENTS` edge. Every prior Kotlin corpus case put the supertype in a separate file or used multi-line bodies, so nothing exercised this shape, and it looked like a resolution-logic gap rather than a parser one. `_recover_collapsed_parse` detects the collapse (only when the initial parse already contains an `ERROR` — a cleanly-parsing file takes none of this path) and splits the pathological body onto two lines before re-parsing, verified by a strict reduction in the tree's total `ERROR` span so an edit that doesn't help is never kept. A line-remap table then reports the original file's line numbers, not the modified buffer's.
